newsitem.title: GERMANY: German growth seen up despite September output fall.
newsitem.headline: German growth seen up despite September output fall.

text.p: The German economy will post higher, export-led growth in the third quarter despite disappointing industrial output in September, economists said Monday.

Private sector economists are expecting third-quarter gross domestic product (GDP) figures, due to be released Wednesday, to show a year-on-year rise close to the 2 percent estimated last month by the economics ministry.
Year-on-year growth in the second quarter was 1.2 percent.
Still, some economists said they had revised their outlook for the economy downwards slightly after preliminary industrial output showed a 1.8 percent fall in September.

"The production figures in September were disappointing, and it is becoming clear that one can't expect any pleasant surprises from the consumer climate at the moment," Bank Julius Baer chief economist Gerhard Grebe said.
Grebe said he had originally been forecasting third-quarter growth of 1 percent over the previous quarter, but had now revised that down to 0.7 percent, for 1.7 percent year-on-year growth.
The quarter-on-quarter growth figure is in any case seen well below the 1.5 percent posted in the second quarter.
